title: Stratified Distribution of Organic Molecules at the Planet-formation Scale in the HH 212 Disk Atmosphere
question: What is the spatial distribution, origin, and formation pathway of formamide (NH2CHO) and related organic molecules (HNCO, H2CO, CH3OH, CH3CHO) in the atmosphere of the HH 212 protostellar disk?

data.sensitivity: continuum: ~ 20 uJy beam^-1 (1.4 K); channel maps: ~ 0.9 mJy beam^-1 (~ 10 K)

what.value: t-HCOOH emission at ~ 346 GHz used for spatial and kinematic comparison

evidence.quote: Looking back at the previous results of other iCOMs detected at higher frequency of $\sim$ 346 GHz (cite: Lee2019COM), we find that t-HCOOH was also detected with the spatial distribution and radial extent consistent with NH$_2$CHO (cite: Lee2019COM).

what.value: Central mass of ~ 0.25 M_sun for Keplerian rotation curves

evidence.quote: Previously, the disk was found to be rotating roughly with a Keplerian rotation due a central mass of $\sim$ 0.25 $M_\odot$ (including the masses of the central protostar and the disk) (cite: Codella2014; Lee2017COM).

what.value: Collisional coefficients of methanol with para-H2 between 10 and 200 K for J<=15

evidence.loc: Physical Properties in the Disk Atmosphere
evidence.quote: We used the collisional coefficients of methanol with para-H$_2$, computed by (cite: Rabli2010) between 10 and 200 K for the J$\leq$15 levels and provided by the BASECOL database (cite: Dubernet2012; Dubernet2013).

what.value: Dusty disk model providing mean H2 column density (~ 1.08 x 10^25 cm^-2), dust continuum optical depth, and temperature structure

evidence.loc: Physical Properties in the Disk Atmosphere
evidence.quote: In addition, the abundance of these molecules are also estimated by dividing the column density of the molecules by the mean H$_2$ column density derived from a dusty disk model (cite: Lee2021Pdisk) in the same region, which is found to be $\sim$ 1.08$\times 10^{25}$ cm$^{-2}$.

what.value: [12C]/[13C] ratio of ~ 50 in the Orion Complex

evidence.loc: Physical Properties in the Disk Atmosphere
evidence.quote: Indeed, the H$_2$CO column density can be better derived from the H$_2$$^{13}$CO line assuming \[$^{12}$C\]/\[$^{13}$C\] ratio of $\sim$ 50, as estimated in the Orion Complex (cite: Kahane2018).

what.value: Binding energies and sublimation temperatures of molecules on amorphous solid water ice

evidence.loc: Distribution of Molecules and Binding Energy
evidence.quote: For consistent comparison, we adopt the values obtained from similar methods on amorphous solid water ice (cite: Ferrero2020; Ferrero2022). Since HNCO was not included in those studies, we adopt its value from (cite: Song2016).

what.value: Line properties from Splatalogue (CDMS and JPL)

evidence.quote: Line Properties from Splatalogue

recipe.goal: Stack molecular lines by upper energy level and produce total intensity maps and PV diagrams
recipe.method: Divide detected lines into two ranges of upper level energies (E_u < 120 K and E_u > 120 K), stack them to produce mean channel maps, then integrate to get total line intensity maps and extract position-velocity (PV) diagrams across the upper and lower disk atmospheres
key_parameters: E_u < 120 K and E_u > 120 K energy bins

recipe.goal: Measure vertical heights and outer disk radii of molecules
recipe.method: Measure vertical height along the jet axis in the lower atmosphere using E_u < 120 K maps; determine outer disk radius from linear PV structures in the upper disk atmosphere where they intersect the Keplerian rotation curve
assumptions: Keplerian rotation around a central mass of ~ 0.25 M_sun

recipe.goal: Derive CH3OH physical properties via non-LTE LVG modeling and rotation diagram
recipe.method: Non-LTE Large Velocity Gradient (LVG) modeling of 7 CH3OH lines with E_u < 200 K at the lower disk atmosphere peak using GRELVG, combined with LTE rotation diagram linear fit of 5 CH3OH lines with E_u > 200 K, then taking the mean of the two methods
key_parameters: N(A-CH3OH) and N(E-CH3OH) varied from 2x10^15 to 1x10^19 cm^-2 (step factor of 2); n_H2 from 10^6 to 10^9 cm^-3 (step factor of 2); T from 50 to 120 K (step of 5 K); linewidth = 4 km s^-1
assumptions: A-/E- CH3OH ratio = 1; semi-infinite slab geometry; 40% measurement uncertainty; optically thin and LTE for E_u > 200 K lines

recipe.goal: Derive excitation temperatures, column densities, and abundances for NH2CHO, HNCO, H2CO, D2CO, H2(13)CO, and CH3CHO
recipe.method: Measure integrated line intensities averaged over a 68 au x 20 au (0.17" x 0.05") rectangular region in the lower atmosphere with a 2 sigma cutoff; fit LTE rotation diagrams for NH2CHO, HNCO, and CH3CHO (with T fixed to 100 K); calculate column densities for H2CO, D2CO, and H2(13)CO at assumed temperatures; divide by model H2 column density to obtain abundances
key_parameters: Rectangular region size 68 au x 20 au (0.17" x 0.05"); cutoff of 2 sigma
assumptions: Optically thin emission and LTE; T_ex = 92 K for D2CO, 60 K for H2CO and H2(13)CO, 100 K for CH3CHO; [12C]/[13C] = 50; H2 column density = 1.08 x 10^25 cm^-2; 40% line intensity uncertainty

score_reason: ALMA project code, calibration CASA version, calibrators, robust weightings, synthesized beams, noise levels, and complete line tables with integrated intensities are clearly provided, allowing direct reproduction of the rotation diagrams; however, imaging parameters, line stacking details, exact extraction region coordinates, and the GRELVG code are not fully specified.
